summary: Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar worked in indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Mumbai and served on the faculty at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1939 to 1955.

Tryambakarama Sastri, a scholar of indology and philosophy, studied at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, under Lakshmana Sastri Dravida. He is attested in 1932 as headmaster at Government Sanskrit Pathashala, Jamnagar.
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk was a scholar who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Active in religious studies, Trịnh Xuân Thuận studied at the California Institute of Technology (circa 1967–1970), Princeton University (circa 1970–1974), and the University of Virginia, where he held a post circa 1976.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Tse-fu Kuan completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Oxford in 2004 under Richard Gombrich. He held a postdoctoral post at National Cheng Kung University and a position attested at Yuan Ze University in 2015.

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Geshe Lharampa at Ganden Monastery, served at Ganden Jangtse Monastery, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Alexander Berzin, Joseph Loizzo, and Thubten Chodron.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang works in Tibetology and linguistics. Educated at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow (1987), he served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and became Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford in 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under the traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD at SOAS, where he also held research posts (attested 1997, 1999–2002). He taught at Oxford and joined UBC as a Research Chair circa 2005.

Tsewang Gyurme is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested in 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Young Lamas Home School. He was master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1975–2020) and taught Andreas Doctor and Phakchok Rinpoche.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Khampagar Monastery and under Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Dilgo Khyentse, Tulku Urgyen, Nyoshul Khenpo, and Adeu Rinpoche. He founded Pundarika Foundation and served at Tergar Osel Ling.

Tsu-lin Mei worked in linguistics and sinology. Educated at Oberlin College, Harvard University, and Yale University, he held academic positions at Harvard University (~1964–1971) and Cornell University (~1971–2000).

A linguist and Tibetologist, Tsuguhito Takeuchi earned degrees from Kyoto University and Indiana University Bloomington under Christopher I. Beckwith and Tatsuo Nishida, among others. He was Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo specialized in Buddhist studies and indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University, he was president of Reiyukai and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and held positions at Rissho University and ICPBS.
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), where she was supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti and studied under Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is an indologist and historian who earned undergraduate and graduate degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

Tsultrim Allione is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar with a master's from Antioch University. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu, and founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987) and as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Tsultrim Kelsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held lecturer and professorial posts at Otani University (attested 1984, 1999–2002) and served as a researcher at Ryukoku University and the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center in 2015.
